brief: The note (The Market Ear, incorporating GS derivatives desk views) argues equity index vol has risen but stays low in absolute terms, while oil vol, skew, VVIX and JPY vol are rising sharply and realized correlation sits at record lows, cross-asset signals suggesting the repricing has further to run given CPI, a yen carry unwind and a potential correlation comeback, so optionality is still cheap. GS's derivatives desk sees a window to add convexity both ways, right-tail AI exposure and near-term macro protection, citing NDX one-month ATM vol compression from roughly 57 to 40 and 20-year-flat put/call skew despite CPI, the GS tech conference and earnings ahead, with the market pricing just a 0.91% weekly move. GS also flags the S&P's lowest-ever six-month realized correlation as historically unsustainable, typically preceding an explosive return of vol. Separately, oil vol and skew are rising while VIX lags, a brutal JPY move raises carry-unwind spillover risk, and IWM puts are flagged as cheap CPI protection with small-cap vol near three-year lows. The note stays long VIX into a three-day weekend as VVIX surges, keeping the October 18/28 VIX call spread its favored structure.
